citations.quote:
Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Let $1\le q\le n$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ be $C^1$ in the sense of [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. Suppose $F(x_*)=0$ and some $q\times q$ minor of the derivative matrix $DF(x_*)$ is invertible. This nonsingular-minor hypothesis is the explicit full-row-rank condition used here. If $q<n$, then after permuting coordinates $x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n-q}\times\mathbb R^q$, there are open neighborhoods $P$ of $u_*$ and $Q$ of $v_*$ and a unique $C^1$ map $\varphi:P\to Q$ such that

$$F(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\varphi(u)\qquad((u,v)\in P\times Q).$$

Its derivative is

$$D\varphi(u)=-D_vF(u,\varphi(u))^{-1}D_uF(u,\varphi(u)).$$

Thus the local zero set is a graph over $n-q$ free coordinates. If $q=n$, the zero is locally isolated, so the local graph dimension is zero. Here “local graph dimension $k$” means a local graph parameterized by an open subset of $\mathbb R^k$, with a singleton counted as dimension zero.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable. For $x,y\in U$, suppose the whole segment $[x,y]$ lies in $U$ and its concavity inequality holds:

$$f(x+t(y-x))\ge(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)\qquad(0\le t\le1).$$

Then the supporting bound is $f(y)\le f(x)+Df(x)(y-x)$. In particular this bound holds for every $x,y$ in any convex subset of $U$ on which $f$ is concave. No global convexity of $U$ is assumed.

Let $A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ be linear, $b\in\mathbb R^k$, and $F=U\cap\{x:Ax=b\}$. Suppose $x_*\in F$, $Df(x_*)h=0$ for every $h\in\ker A$, and for every $y\in F$ the segment $[x_*,y]$ lies in $U$ and has the displayed concavity inequality. Then $x_*$ is a global maximum of $f$ on $F$. If $F$ is convex and $f|_F$ is strictly concave, meaning the inequality is strict for distinct endpoints and $0<t<1$, the maximum is unique.

For the curvature clause, suppose $f\in C^2(U)$ and fix $x\in U$. If, for every $h\in\mathbb R^d$, all sufficiently small $|t|$ satisfy $x\pm th\in U$ and

$$f(x+th)+f(x-th)\le2f(x),$$

then the Hessian bilinear form $D^2f(x)=D(Df)(x)$ satisfies $D^2f(x)[h,h]\le0$ for every $h$. This condition holds whenever $f$ is concave on a neighborhood of $x$. Thus a $C^2$ function concave on an open convex region has negative-semidefinite Hessian there. Concavity alone does not assert strict curvature.

derivations.claim: The map $(n,s)\mapsto(v,\sigma_p)=(1/n,s/n)$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, so $Y$ is open as the inverse image of $X$. Direct differentiation gives $dv=-dn/n^2$ and $d\sigma_p=ds/n-s\,dn/n^2$.
From $h=\varepsilon+p=n(e+pv)$ and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, we obtain $Ts+\mu n=T(n\sigma_p)+(H-T\sigma_p)n=nH=h=\varepsilon+p$.

The map $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)\mapsto(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)$ is smooth on the open set $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)^2$, so the parcel domain $\mathcal D=\{(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):\mathsf V>0,\mathsf N>0,(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X\}$ is open. The definition of $E$ is a $C^2$ composition. Differentiating it gives
$$\partial_{\mathsf S}E=e_{\sigma_p}=T,\quad \partial_{\mathsf V}E=e_v=-p,\quad \partial_{\mathsf N}E=e-v e_v-\sigma_p e_{\sigma_p}=e+pv-T\sigma_p=\mu.$$
Thus $dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N$.

For the heat-capacity clause, define $F(v,\sigma_p,T)=e_{\sigma_p}(v,\sigma_p)-T$. This is $C^1$, vanishes at the given state with $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, and its derivative in $\sigma_p$ is $e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$. By [F2] its zero set is locally a unique $C^1$ graph $\sigma_p=\varphi(v,T)$. Differentiating at fixed $v$ gives $\partial_T\sigma_p=1/e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}$, whence $c_v=e_{\sigma_p}\partial_T\sigma_p=T/e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$.

For the compressibility clause, define $G(v,\sigma_p,p)=p(v,\sigma_p)-p=-e_v(v,\sigma_p)-p$. It is $C^1$ and its derivative in $v$ is $-e_{vv}<0$. By [F2], $v$ is a local $C^1$ function of $(\sigma_p,p)$, with $(\partial v/\partial p)_{\sigma_p}=-1/e_{vv}$. Therefore $\kappa_{\sigma_p}=1/(v e_{vv})>0$.

At fixed $\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon(n,\sigma_p)=n e(1/n,\sigma_p)$ and $p(n,\sigma_p)=-e_v(1/n,\sigma_p)$. Differentiating gives $\partial_n\varepsilon=e-e_v/n=e+p/n=h/n$ and $\partial_np=e_{vv}/n^2$. Since $h/n>0$ by [A3], the local implicit-rank theorem makes $\varepsilon$ a valid local coordinate in place of $n$. Taking the ratio of the two derivatives yields $\alpha_{\sigma_p}=e_{vv}/(nh)>0$.

By the chain rule, $de=e_v\,dv+e_{\sigma_p}\,d\sigma_p=-p\,dv+T\,d\sigma_p$. Since $\varepsilon=ne$, the product rule and step 1.1 give
$$d\varepsilon=e\,dn+n\,de=T\,ds+\left(e+\frac{p}{n}-T\sigma_p\right)dn=T\,ds+\mu\,dn.$$
Here $v=1/n$, so $e+p/n-T\sigma_p=H-T\sigma_p=\mu$.

For $\lambda>0$, $E(\lambda\mathsf S,\lambda\mathsf V,\lambda\mathsf N)=\lambda E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$ because the intensive ratios are unchanged. Differentiating this identity in $\lambda$ at $1$ yields $E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N$. At $z_0=(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, differentiate Euler's identity $DE(z_0)[z_0]=E(z_0)$ in an arbitrary direction $w$. The two first-derivative terms cancel, leaving $D^2E(z_0)[w,z_0]=0$ for every $w$; symmetry of the Hessian gives $D^2E(z_0)[z_0,w]=0$.
Differentiating $\varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n$ and substituting step 2.1 cancels $T\,ds$ and $\mu\,dn$, leaving $dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu$.

Apply [F4] to $-e$, which is concave when $e$ is convex on the convex open domain $X$. Its Hessian is $-D^2e$ and is negative semidefinite, so $D^2e$ is positive semidefinite. This conditional curvature statement does not promote the response inequalities to convexity without [A4].

risk_review.notes: Independently checked all ten proof steps and four exact suppliers, including open-domain implicit-rank graph theorem and concave-Hessian clause. Y and parcel domain are open; n,v,N are strictly positive, so all divisions and compositions are defined. C2 e gives required C1 response maps. Chain/product rules yield Gibbs, Euler and Gibbs-Duhem identities; the parcel domain is invariant under every positive scaling, and differentiating Euler gives radial Hessian kernel without any global spacetime extensivity claim. Response minors are respectively e_sigma_sigma, -e_vv and h/n, nonzero under the exact separate assumptions; their ratios and positive signs agree. No response is asserted at vanishing minors, nor does diagonal positivity imply convexity. Applied concave-Hessian supplier to -e only under convex X and convex e. Reader/refuter comma-space finding confirmed nonfatal and repaired in title only; Statement and proof unchanged.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Then there is an open
neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ of $p$ and a smooth future-directed tetrad field
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $U$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]), i.e.
$g_q(E_A(q),E_B(q))=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$ for all $q\in U$ with
$E_0(q)$ future-directed for every $q\in U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For every vector $X$, $u_a(\Delta X)^a=u_aX^a+(u_au^a)(u_bX^b)=0$ and $\Delta u=0$. If $X\in u^\perp$, then $\Delta X=X$. Hence $\operatorname{im}\Delta=u^\perp$, $\ker\Delta=\mathbb Ru$, and $\Delta^2=\Delta$. Also $g(\Delta X,Y)=g(X,Y)+g(X,u)g(u,Y)=g(X,\Delta Y)$ for all $X,Y$, so $\Delta$ is self-adjoint and is the orthogonal projection onto $u^\perp$.

Since $\delta^a{}_c=\Delta^a{}_c-u^a u_c$, expansion in both indices gives
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd}-u^a u_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd}-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d\,u^b+u^a u^b u_cu_d\mathsf T^{cd}.$$
By the definitions this is the stated decomposition. Orthogonality of $Q$ and $P$ follows by $u_a\Delta^a{}_c=0$, so $\pi$ is spatial as well. Since $g_{ab}\Delta^{ab}=3$, the definition of $p_{\mathrm{mech}}$ gives $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. The component formulas recover $\varepsilon_u,Q,P$ from any such decomposition, so it is unique.

In the chosen tetrad of [F3], identify symmetric contravariant tensors with the ten-dimensional vector space $\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^4)$ and write $T^A{}_B=\mathsf T^{AC}\eta_{CB}$ for their mixed components. For $w\in\mathbb B^3$, put $\gamma(w)=(1-|w|^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\widehat u^A(w)=\gamma(w)(1,w^1,w^2,w^3)$, the tetrad components of $u(x,w)$ from clause 4, and define
$$\Phi_i(T,w):=T^i{}_A\widehat u^A(w)-w^iT^0{}_A\widehat u^A(w)\quad(i=1,2,3).$$
This is a smooth map on the open subset $\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^4)\times\mathbb B^3\cong\mathbb R^{10}\times\mathbb B^3$ of $\mathbb R^{13}$, and $\Phi(T_0,0)=0$. At $T_0=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon_0,p_0,p_0,p_0)$ as a contravariant matrix, the mixed matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-\varepsilon_0,p_0,p_0,p_0)$. Since $\partial_{w^j}\widehat u^0(0)=0$ and $\partial_{w^j}\widehat u^k(0)=\delta^k_j$, direct differentiation gives $\partial_{w^j}\Phi_i(T_0,0)=p_0\delta_{ij}+\varepsilon_0\delta_{ij}=h_0\delta_{ij}$. Thus $D_w\Phi(T_0,0)=h_0I_3$ is invertible by $h_0>0$.

Put $
u_u=-u\cdot J$. Then $J-
u_u u=J+u(u\cdot J)=\Delta J=V$, and [step 1.1] shows $V\in u^\perp$. If $J=
u u+W$ with $W\perp u$, contracting with $u$ forces $
u=
u_u$ and applying $\Delta$ forces $W=V$.

$Q=0$ is equivalent to $\Delta(\mathsf T^\sharp u)=0$, where $(\mathsf T^\sharp u)^a:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_b$. By [step 1.1], $\ker\Delta=\mathbb Ru$, so this holds exactly when $\mathsf T^a{}_b u^b$ is a scalar multiple of $u^a$, the timelike-eigenvector condition.

Apply [F2] with $q=3$ to $\Phi(T,w)=0$. The $3\times3$ minor in the $w$ variables is invertible by step 1.3, so near $(T_0,0)$ the zero set is a unique $C^1$ graph $w=\varphi(T)$. Choose an open ball $W\subset\mathbb B^3$ about $0$ within the graph neighborhood and shrink the tensor neighborhood so that $\varphi(T)\in W$. In the chosen tetrad, the component map $x\mapsto T^A{}_B(x)$ is $C^1$, because $\mathsf T$ is $C^1$ and the tetrad is smooth. Shrink to a neighborhood $U\subset O_0$ on which these components remain in that tensor neighborhood; then $w_L(x):=\varphi(T(x))$ is $C^1$, and $u_L(x):=u(x,w_L(x))$ is a $C^1$ future unit timelike field. The equations $\Phi_i(T(x),w_L(x))=0$ say that the spatial components of $\mathsf T^A{}_B(x)u_L^B(x)$ equal $w_L^i(x)$ times its time component, so $\mathsf T^A{}_B(x)u_L^B(x)=\lambda(x)u_L^A(x)$ for a scalar $\lambda(x)$. By step 2.2 this is equivalent to $Q_{u_L(x)}(x)=0$, and uniqueness of the local graph gives the claimed uniqueness of $w_L$.

Let $r:=\sqrt{-g(J,J)}>0$. Then $u_E=J/r$ is future unit timelike and $\Delta_{u_E}J=J+u_E(u_E\cdot J)=J+(J/r)(-r)=0$. Conversely, if a future unit timelike $u$ has $\Delta_uJ=0$, step 2.1 gives $J=\lambda u$ for a scalar $\lambda$. Since both $J$ and $u$ are future timelike, $\lambda>0$; hence $-g(J,J)=\lambda^2$ forces $\lambda=r$ and $u=u_E$.

If $g(\ell,u)=0$, then $\ell\in u^\perp$, and [F4] makes the restricted metric positive definite; since $g(\ell,\ell)=0$, this would force $\ell=0$. Therefore $g(\ell,u)\ne0$, so $\mathsf T^\sharp u=\rho\ell\,g(\ell,u)$ is a nonzero null vector. It cannot equal $\lambda u$ for any scalar $\lambda$: if $\lambda=0$ it is nonzero, and if $\lambda\ne0$ the right side is timelike while the left side is null. Thus no timelike eigenvector exists.

citations.quote:
Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

The local response statements are conditional. At a state with $T>0$ and $e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$, temperature is a valid local coordinate at fixed $v$, and the per-marker heat capacity
$$c_v:=\left(\frac{\partial e}{\partial T}\right)_v=\frac{T}{e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$, the isentropic compressibility
$$\kappa_{\sigma_p}:=-\frac1v\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac1{v e_{vv}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$ and $h>0$, the local pressure-energy response
$$\alpha_{\sigma_p}:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n h}$$
is positive. If $X$ is convex and $e$ is convex on $X$, then $D^2e$ is positive semidefinite. Positivity of the displayed diagonal responses is not asserted to imply convexity, a sound cone, or an evolution theorem.

derivations.claim: Since $mc^2$ is constant in $(v,\sigma_p)$, $(e_m)_{\sigma_p}=(e_0)_{\sigma_p}$ and $-(e_m)_v=-(e_0)_v$. Thus the derived temperature and pressure are unchanged.
The definitions give $H_m=e_m+p_mv=H_0+mc^2$ and $\mu_m=H_m-T_m\sigma_p=\mu_0+mc^2$.
With $n=1/v$ unchanged, $\varepsilon_m=ne_m=\varepsilon_0+nmc^2$ and $h_m=\varepsilon_m+p_m=h_0+nmc^2$.

At fixed $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, the parcel construction gives $E_m=E_0+\mathsf Nmc^2$. Differentiating adds only $mc^2\,d\mathsf N$ to $dE_0$; hence at fixed marker count it changes neither the entropy derivative $T$ nor the pressure-work derivative $-p$. This agrees with the chemical-potential shift in step 2.1 and the parcel first law in [F2].
